title: Why build them
summary: The Lab's thesis cut to three short paragraphs and one conclusion: the kit's one-line section head across the top, the essay in the right half beneath it, and the conclusion last, in display type under a hairline.
story: The still beat after the board. The header showed what exists; this says why it is worth building, in the reader's own terms (a CRM that only records, five tools with no shared memory, a generic model that writes your competitors' sentences), and only then lands on the page's thesis: instruments for each layer we install, inside a system the client owns. Question → reasons → answer, in reading order. It hands over to the ledger, which reads the board row by row.
copy: [N] Label “The reasoning” (was “Why build them”, which repeated the h2)
[N] h2 “Why an advisory firm builds instruments.” (answers the side question “are they a software company?”)
[R from T·01] “A CRM records what happened. It doesn’t decide what happens next.”
[R from T·03] “Data vendor, sequencer, enrichment, dialer, notes: five tools with no shared memory. Whatever a motion learns is scattered across them.” (the count is fixed: five)

[R from T·04] “A generic model writes the same sentences for you as for your competitors. The useful instrument is one trained on what an engagement teaches — anonymised and aggregated, as the engagement agreement spells out.”
[R] Conclusion “So the Lab builds instruments for each layer we install, inside a system the client owns.”
Cut, per the story map: “the end of GTM software”, “a filing cabinet wearing a dashboard”, “mathematically dead” (T·02), “or it’s autocomplete”
